The server now gives a different key for “%1$s”. It may be a reinstall — or an impostor. Sending is paused until you compare safety numbers in person or over video.

The key of “%1$s” came from the server — and the server could have handed you its own. Once the same key has stood in the public key log for a day, the app confirms it by itself. Or scan their safety number code in person, or compare it over video. Until then you can read, but not write.
“%1$s” now uses a different key. This conversation stays readable; new messages go to the chat with the current key.
Enter your PIN to decrypt your messages
Wrong PIN. The next attempt is delayed
Compare these 60 digits with the other person face to face or over video. If they match, your conversation is protected against key substitution.
Not verified — compare the safety number
An end-to-end encrypted messenger. Starting a conversation is protected against future quantum computers too.
Not independently audited. Do not rely on it where life or liberty is at stake.
Latin letters, digits and _. This is how others will find you.
Setting things up — this takes a few seconds…
3–32 characters: lowercase Latin letters, digits and _, starting with a letter
Connections go through Tor, built into the app, so the server does not see your IP address. The first connection takes up to a minute.
Direct connection: messages stay end-to-end encrypted, but the server sees your IP address. Turn Tor on to hide it; you can change this later in Settings.
Could not connect through Tor. Check your internet connection and try again, or turn Tor off.
Couldn’t find this person. Check the name and your connection.
It encrypts your messages on this device. There is no way to reset it.
The PIN must be exactly 6 digits
Profile QR code: show it to someone so they can add you
The link carries your key, like the QR code: whoever pastes it into “New chat” can write to you right away. Send it over a channel you trust.
Write to me in GasApp. Paste this link into “New chat”:\n%1$s
“%1$s” was already in your contacts with a different key. It may be a reinstall — or an impostor. Compare safety numbers in person before messaging them.
This is your own code — show it to the person you want to talk to
Add someone by username or by scanning their QR code.
Sending. Photos, videos and audio are sent without location, camera model or file name — but a document keeps its own metadata, such as the author and the program it was made in.
The file is larger than 100 MB
The file was changed on the server and was not opened
Until the key is compared, you cannot be sure you are talking to the person this contact claims to be.
Calls are not available in this version
When calls arrive, they will be end-to-end encrypted, like your messages
The message disappears for you right away, and for the other person once the request reaches them. They have already seen the text and may remember it.
Turn on: the other person will see when you have read their messages
The other person sees when you have read their messages
The other person sees when you were last online
Keeps your messages out of screenshots and the recent apps preview
Show the message on the lock screen

Blocking screenshots only works on this device. It does not stop someone from photographing the screen with another phone, and it does not restrict the other person: they saw your message and could have saved it.
Use your fingerprint instead of typing the PIN

The PIN cannot be reset: without it, the messages on this device cannot be decrypted — not by us either. You can erase this device’s data and get your account back with your recovery key: your username and the conversations from your last backup return, newer messages are lost. Without a recovery key the account cannot be returned.
Fingerprints on this device have changed, so fingerprint unlock was turned off. Enter your PIN; you can turn it back on in Privacy.
Skip typing the PIN. The PIN still works and is still what protects your messages — your fingerprint only unlocks a sealed copy of the key.
Off by default. For people who fear the phone being taken and the PIN guessed. Only your recovery key can bring the data back.

After ten wrong PINs in a row, all messages, contacts and vault files on this phone are erased — including when a child or a pocket types them. Without a recovery key they cannot be brought back, not even by us.
Could not turn on fingerprint unlock. Your PIN still works.
Wrong PIN — fingerprint unlock is not turned on.
Add a fingerprint in system settings first.
This device has no strong fingerprint sensor.

You will get a JSON file with your username, contacts, conversations and settings.

⚠️ The file is NOT encrypted. Anyone who gets it can read every message in it. Save it somewhere you control, and delete it when you are done.

Keys are never included, so this file cannot restore your account — use a backup for that.
Data exported. Remember: the file is not encrypted.
Removes your account from the server and everything stored for it on this device. There is no way back.

Your username, keys and any undelivered messages will be removed from the server, and this device will be wiped — every conversation, contact and file.\n\nWhat this does not do: messages already delivered stay on your contacts\u2019 devices, and files sent to you stay on the server until they expire after 30 days. Your username becomes available for anyone else to take — they cannot pose as you, because their key would be different and your contacts would be warned.
Nobody can restore this account — not you, not whoever runs the server. If you only want to sign out of this device, close the app instead.
The account was not deleted. Nothing on this device has been touched — check your connection and try again.
The account is gone from the server, but something on this device could not be removed. Uninstall the app to be sure.
Show the message on the lock screen
Show who the message came from

Push notifications are not available yet: new messages arrive while the app is open, or the next time you open it. Once push is added, the server will send only a “something new” signal — no text, no sender and no chat.
The app is designed for a dark background. A light theme would mean a second palette and a second chance to get the color of a security state wrong — so there isn\'t one.
English is the default. Russian is also available.
Deletion cannot be undone: the server keeps no copies, so there is nothing to restore from.
Every linked device can read all of your messages. Device linking will come with multi-device sync; for now, your account works only on this device.
The protocol version determines compatibility: someone on an older version will not be able to read your message. The client is Apache-2.0, the server is AGPL-3.0.
Your backup is encrypted with a recovery key. Only you have that key: neither we nor the server can decrypt the backup.
Earlier backups stay encrypted with the old key — the app cannot re-encrypt them. Keep the old key for as long as you need those backups.
If you lose this key, your data cannot be recovered. Not even by us. There is no reset by email or SMS — and that is exactly why nobody else can read your messages.
Write this key down on paper and keep it away from your phone. It decrypts all of your backups.
The key is shown only once. The app does not keep it, so you will not be able to look it up later.
Screenshots are blocked here: a key in a screenshot would land in your gallery, and from there in the cloud.
I have written the key down
Enter three groups from the key you wrote down. This check is here so you don\'t lose access to your own data: without the key, it cannot be recovered.
The groups did not match. Check them against what you wrote down.

Pick the backup files in the order they were made: the full snapshot first, then the increments. If a file in the middle is missing, nothing is restored. The app cannot check for the newest files: without them, the restore still succeeds but brings back an older state — including messages you deleted later.
There is a typo in the key
Restore failed: wrong key, or files are missing from the chain
Messages, contacts and settings will be restored. Disappearing messages are not in backups. This device will get a new security key — that is normal, and we\'ll explain why.
Records restored: %1$d. Your backup is as of %2$s. If you backed up later than that, some files were missing: restore again with all of them — otherwise messages you deleted since may be back.
Your contacts will see a warning that your security key changed. After a restore this is normal: the device gets a new key, and the old one is not carried over.

Keys are not carried over on purpose. Moving the old encryption state across would mean two different messages could be encrypted with the same key — and that reveals what they say. A changed security key is the price of that never happening.
Not restored: active secure sessions — they will be set up again with the first message — and backups: create a new recovery key in Settings → Backup, otherwise no new backups will be made.
The vault is protected by a second factor. Even when the app is unlocked, you have to confirm it\'s you again to reach the files.
Enter all six digits of your PIN
The vault closes after a minute of inactivity and whenever the app goes into the background.
Closes after a minute of inactivity, or when the app goes into the background.

The encrypted copy is in the vault. The original is still in your phone’s shared storage, where the gallery, other apps and cloud backup can see it. Deleting it does not remove a copy that was already backed up to the cloud.
The original could not be deleted from here — delete it in the app where it is stored
Sealed sender on for every message
IP address hidden by a proxy or Tor
Without it the phone is open to anyone who picks it up
Signs of rooting found — other apps may be able to read your data
Storage key held in secure hardware
In StrongBox, a separate security chip
Hardware key protection is not available on this device: the key is stored in software, and a copy of the app’s files is protected only by your PIN
The bootloader is unlocked or the system did not pass verified boot: the system may have been replaced, and its other answers cannot be trusted
The confirmation does not come from Google’s root: an emulator, an uncertified phone or a forgery
App signed by the GasApp developers
This copy is signed by someone else. It may have been modified — install GasApp from an official source
Not checked: this is a development build
Without Tor or a proxy, the server sees your device\'s IP address: it reveals roughly where you are and can link your accounts to each other. Tor, built into the app, hides it.
The server sees your IP address.
All requests and notifications go through the proxy you specify. If it is unreachable, the app will not connect — it will not fall back to a direct connection.
The server will see your IP address: roughly where you are, and which of your accounts share a network. Tor hides it.
Saved. New connections use the method you chose.
The address or port is not valid. Enter a hostname or IP address without a scheme or path; usernames and passwords are not supported.
A proxy can see that you use GasApp, and when. Tor hides your address from the server, but not from the Tor entry node. Over Tor the connection is less stable, and notifications may arrive late.
The network setting is corrupted — connections are blocked until you choose a connection method again.
Proxy and Tor need Android 7.0 or newer: on older versions the system does not guarantee that the hostname goes through the proxy, and the address would leak over DNS.
Delete “%1$s”? There is no copy anywhere, and it cannot be recovered.
A contact’s post-quantum key differs from the one you knew
A known username arrived with a different key
A new contact key was accepted without comparing
The server\'s sealed sender key changed
A recipient rejected your access key
A sender certificate did not match its key
A conversation started without the other person\'s one-time key
A replayed start of an old conversation was rejected
You have not talked before. Until you accept, they get no read receipts and do not see you typing. Declining deletes the conversation, and they are not told.
The conversation will be deleted on this device. The other person is not notified and does not learn that you read it.
Request sent. The conversation starts when they accept or reply.
Restore my account from a backup
Your username and conversations come back from the backup. Your security key will be new, so the people you talk to need to compare safety numbers with you again.
Could not restore the account. Check the backup key and your connection. Backups made before this version do not contain an account recovery key.
Tor runs inside the app — nothing to install. Until it connects, the app does not connect either: it never falls back to a direct connection.
Connecting to Tor is taking long (%1$d%%). Check your internet connection.

If Tor does not connect, it may be blocked where you are. Add WebTunnel bridges, one per line: get them at bridges.torproject.org (choose WebTunnel) or from the Telegram bot @GetBridgesBot. Leave empty to connect to Tor directly.
A bridge line is not valid. Only WebTunnel and plain bridges are supported, and each needs its fingerprint.
The phone\'s secure key storage did not respond. Unlock the phone, restart it if needed, and try again. Your PIN was not checked.
The key that protects your messages is gone from this phone\'s secure storage. The messages on this device cannot be opened any more. Use “Forgot PIN?” to start over and restore from a backup.
The date or time on this device is wrong, so the server rejects requests. Set the time automatically and try again.
Tor is not connecting — it may be blocked here. Tap to add a bridge.
Key checked by the key log — compare in person for full certainty
The server showed a different key under your name. Your contacts may have been sent to someone else — warn them in person
The server’s key log did not match what it showed before
A contact sees a different server key log than you do. The server may be showing one of you a fake one — compare safety numbers in person
Unreadable incoming messages were discarded (repeats of old ones or junk)
The server key log is available, but checking your own name in it keeps failing. Until it succeeds, ask contacts to compare safety numbers in person
Point the camera at the QR code in the other person’s GasApp profile
Point the camera at the safety number code on the other person’s screen
The camera is needed only to read the code. Frames are processed on this device and are never stored or sent anywhere.

If the account is more than a day old, you can write right away: the key is checked by the public key log. Scanning their QR code in person is the strongest check. A contact link (gasapp://contact/…), such as the one a bot’s author publishes, can be pasted here too.
The code carries their key directly, bypassing the server — you can write immediately.
This is not a GasApp contact code, or the name in it belongs to a different key
This is how people find you in GasApp
Show this code to the person next to you — they scan it in GasApp. It carries your key, so they can write to you right away: the strongest check.

The other person’s screen shows a different key. The server may have swapped it, or this is not the person you think. Do not mark them as compared and do not send anything important until you find out why.
Messages are encrypted on your phone. The server only passes them on and cannot read them.
No phone number. An account is a username and an email address — the server keeps only a hash of the address.
Tor is built in: turn it on and the server does not see your IP address.
People will find you by your username. The email is only for confirming the account: we will send a code to it.
The PINs do not match. Enter a new PIN again.
Tor is blocked here — connecting through bridges… %1$d%%
Their messages will stop arriving, and you will not be able to write to them. They are not told. Only this phone knows about the block — not the server.
Their messages do not arrive, and you cannot write to them.
The server operator gets proof that this account wrote to you — not your conversation: the server does not have it. %1$s is not told.
You have already reported this account.
You can report once they have sent you a message.
Could not send the report. Check the connection and try again.
This copy of GasApp may be fake

This app is not signed by the GasApp developers. Someone may have modified it to read your messages or steal your PIN. Delete it and install GasApp only from the official store page or the project site.
Confirm it is you: this action cannot be left to whoever holds your unlocked phone.
This is not the key of your backups. Enter the recovery key you wrote down, or create a new one.
This PIN is too easy to guess: such PINs are tried first. Choose another one.
A contact was blocked on this device
A contact was reported to the server operator
Sending the code to your email
We will send a confirmation code here. The server does not store the address itself, only its hash; the mail service that delivers the code does see it.
That does not look like an email address
This email already has an account. To get it back, restore it from a backup.
Could not send the code. Check your connection; a new email can be requested once a minute.
We sent a 6-digit code to %1$s. It is valid for 15 minutes.
No email? Check the spam folder. You can leave the app to read it — your place here is kept.
A new code is on its way. The previous one no longer works.
The code did not match or has expired. After five wrong tries a code stops working — request a new one.
Point the camera at the channel QR code
A channel is opened by its invitation link. For a closed channel the link sends a join request, which whoever runs the channel approves.
This is not a channel link
Could not open the channel: no connection to the server, or the channel was deleted.
No connection to the server. Try again.
A channel is a feed from one author. Add one by its link, QR code or \@name. The server sees which channels your account follows; it cannot read channels that have no public name.
The server stores the title and the posts encrypted. Anyone who has the channel link can read them.
Title: up to 64 characters. Description: up to 500.
Only premium accounts can create channels and bots; reading channels is open to everyone. Premium is granted by the server operator by hand — send them your username: @%1$s
Only the author can post here
The channel key has changed. To read new posts, ask whoever runs the channel for an invitation link and send a request.
The post was not published: no connection to the server. Your text is still here.
Write the first post, then share the channel link.
The author has not posted anything yet.
This link is the access itself: whoever gets it reads the whole channel, past and future posts. It cannot be revoked for one reader.
The channel and all its posts will be removed from the server for everyone. Readers keep what they have already loaded. This cannot be undone.
The channel and its posts will be removed from this phone. You can add it again by its link.

resources.string: That post is not on this phone yet. Scroll up to load older posts.
The reaction was not saved: no connection to the server.
Readers will see the post marked as edited. Those who already loaded it keep the old text until they sync.
The post and its files are removed from the server and, at their next sync, from readers\' phones. Copies made outside the app stay. This cannot be undone.
The post was not accepted: it is empty, too long, or a file could not be processed.
Could not get the file: no connection, the post was deleted, or the file was changed on the server.
A post holds up to 10 files
The file is larger than %1$d MB
Photos and videos are published without location or camera model. A document keeps its own metadata: author, edit history.
The search runs on this phone, over the posts already loaded. The server does not know the text of the posts.
Nothing found in the loaded posts
Muted: new posts are not counted on the Channels tab

A public channel can be found by its \@name. For that, the server receives the channel link — and with it the read key: the server will be able to read this channel, its posts and files. It still cannot forge your posts. Making the channel private again does not take that knowledge back.
The channel will no longer be found by its name; readers who already have it keep reading. The server has already seen the read key, and that cannot be undone.
3 to 32 characters: Latin letters, digits and _, starting with a letter
This name is taken by another channel
Public channel \@%1$s. The server can read it; it cannot forge the author\'s posts.
Link-only channel: the server stores its title, posts and files encrypted. Anyone who has the link can read it.
Subscribers, views and reactions are counted by the server. Nobody signs these numbers.
Only public channels are found, and only by name: the server does not know the titles of the others.
Enter at least two characters of the name
No public channel with such a name
The server decides which channel a name leads to. If it matters that this is a particular author\'s channel, compare the link with the author.
Your request to be an administrator has not been accepted. Only the owner and administrators post here.

An administrator can publish, edit and delete posts in this channel. The title, the pin, the picture, the public name and the list of administrators stay with you. The name is only for you: readers do not see it.
Point the camera at the QR code on the future administrator\'s phone
This is not a request to administer a channel
The request was not accepted: it is for another channel, or the channel already has 16 administrators.
Removed. The entry stays so that the posts this administrator wrote before can still be read.

The server stops accepting posts from this administrator, and readers stop accepting anything new signed with their key. Posts already written stay. A removed administrator acting together with the server could still rewrite posts published before the removal.
QR code of the request to administer the channel
Show this code to the channel owner or send them the text. There are no secrets in it. If the owner accepts, the server will know that your account administers this channel.

A closed channel is joined by request: you or an administrator approve each person. The server gives posts only to members; current subscribers stay. The channel key changes at once, so the old link no longer opens new posts. Current subscribers keep what they have already read, but to read on they must send a request by your invitation link. When a subscriber is removed, the key changes again. A closed channel cannot be made open again.
Remove the public name first: by its \@name the server hands out a link with the read key, so such a channel cannot be closed.
Anyone who has the channel link will be able to read it again. Join requests will no longer be needed.
Closed channel: joined by request, and the server gives posts only to members. It stores the title, posts and files encrypted.
This channel is closed: invitation links come from whoever runs it
This link sends a join request to the channel. It carries no read key: only those whose request is approved will read the channel.\n\n%1$s
Link revoked: no new requests will come through it
The request is signed with the key of your contact by this name. Whoever you approve gets the channel read key — it cannot be taken back.
Who this is, only the server says: you have no such contact. Whoever you approve gets the channel read key — it cannot be taken back.

The server will stop giving them posts and will not accept a new request from them, and the channel key will change: they will not read new posts. What was published before the removal they could already read.
Whoever runs the channel cannot be removed this way: dismiss them as an administrator first
The ban will be lifted. They become a subscriber only if their new request is approved.
This is a closed channel: it is joined by request. Whoever runs the channel, and the server, will learn your account name. The channel appears in the list once the request is approved.
You were removed from this channel: the request was not accepted
Request not sent: the link was revoked, the channel is gone, or there is no connection
The request will disappear from this phone. If it is approved later, you will not be able to join with it — you will need to send a new one.
A bot is a separate account run by your program: it answers messages and, once made an administrator, posts to a channel, approves requests and removes subscribers. A bot name ends in bot.
Bot name: Latin letters, digits and _, ending in bot
Did not work: no connection to the server, or there are too many bots already
Give this line to the bot program (gasapp-bot). It is valid for an hour and works once; it is not stored here. The bot\'s keys are created where it runs — this phone never sees them.\n\n%1$s
The bot account will disappear: it leaves the channels where it was an administrator, and its program can no longer sign in.
Subscriber removed. The channel key will change as soon as there is a connection
⚠️ A subscriber was removed, but the channel key has not changed yet: there was no connection. It will be retried automatically; until then new posts use the old key.
Did not work: the button is gone or there is no connection
The button and the link were sent by the other person. It will open outside GasApp:\n\n%1$s
Could not open the page: no browser found
By creating an account you accept the Terms of Use and the Privacy Policy. Tap to read them.

The report goes to the server operator together with your account name. The operator cannot read this channel\'s posts unless you give access. “Send with access” attaches the channel link to the report, so the operator can open the channel and see what you are reporting.

You have not verified this person, but their key has stood under this name in the key log for more than a day: the server could not have swapped it unnoticed. Whoever you approve gets the channel read key — it cannot be taken back.
